fieldMarks: Among the largest Asian antelopes: 120-150 cm at the shoulder, stocky body on slender legs.
Adult males blue-gray; females and young yellow-brown to pale brown.
White patches on the face and below the chin and a broad white throat 'bib'; males have a hanging throat tuft up to 13 cm.
Males carry short black horns about 20-25 cm.
White band from the brisket over the belly forming a narrow rump patch outlined in darker hair.
behavior: Usually in herds of about 10, sometimes 20-70.
Most active in early morning and late afternoon.
Eyesight and hearing equal to or better than white-tailed deer, but a poor sense of smell; spooks easily and can run up to 29 mph.
Grazes and browses; in Texas eats mesquite, oak, partridge pea, croton, nightshade and grasses.
habitat: In Texas, South Texas brush country; native habitat is dry grassland, steppe woodland and hillsides in India.
range: Introduced: native to India; released on South Texas ranches around 1930. Most are on large ranches in Kenedy and Willacy counties, Texas.
